_comment: Ranking and classification weights for Evidence Digest. Every number a reader's feed depends on lives here, so ranking can be tuned and reviewed without touching code. The scoring function is deterministic: the same record always yields the same score, and no language model is involved. See contract/config.schema.json for the shape.

classifier._comment: A study joins a topic when its accumulated match points reach assignThreshold. MeSH alone is enough (curated, high precision). A title phrase alone is enough. An abstract-only mention is not - that is what keeps 'we did not study lymphoma' out of the lymphoma feed.

journalTier._comment: Reach of the venue. Deliberately smaller than the evidence-design contribution: a randomized trial in a tier-3 specialty journal should outrank an editorial in a tier-1.

bonuses._comment: Additive signals detected from publication types, MeSH, registry IDs, and conservative regexes over the title and abstract.

penalties._comment: Subtractive signals. Corrections and retraction notices are kept rather than dropped - a retraction is genuinely important news - but they are pushed far down the default ranking and carry their own badge in the UI.
penalties._noAbstract_comment: This is the most load-bearing penalty in the file, and the reason is empirical: across a 7-day sample of newly indexed records from NEJM, Lancet, JAMA, Annals, Blood, JCO and Circulation, only 19% carried an abstract. The other 81% were letters, replies, editorials, errata and - critically - news items that PubMed types as a plain 'Journal Article' with no distinguishing publication type at all ('US Death Rates Reach All-Time Low in 2025'). No publication-type rule can separate those from real research; the absent abstract is the only reliable signal. So a missing abstract is treated as strong evidence that a record is not a substantive study, and the reader-facing surfaces additionally default to hasAbstract=true with an explicit opt-in toggle for correspondence and news.

recency._comment: Exponential decay on PubMed entry date, so a two-week-old paper still ranks but today's leads. halfLifeDays of 10 means a 10-day-old study keeps half its recency points.

limits._comment: Volume guards. All-of-medicine coverage across ~120 journals produces roughly 500-1500 newly indexed records a day, so the served window and per-file caps are what keep the static API small enough to load instantly on a phone.
limits._searchIndexMinScore_comment: Tuned against a real 865-record harvest rather than guessed. The noAbstract penalty separates the corpus cleanly: substantive studies span 16-100 (median 44) while correspondence and news peak at 37 (median 6). A threshold of 35 therefore indexes 73% of substantive studies while admitting essentially no noise - at 55 it covered only 28%, which made the global search box feel broken. Raise it only if the index file becomes a payload problem.
